source_name: State Audit Service of Ukraine (Держаудитслужба) monitoring data via Prozorro/BI
why_relevant: DASU monitoring decisions on specific tenders expose contested procurements, cancellations and re-tenders — signals that an IT or consulting programme at a state bank/agency is delayed or restructured. Accessible as a dataset inside BI Prozorro.

source_name: Prozorro tender page pattern — direct per-tender records
why_relevant: Individual tender pages carry the payload the cell needs: technical requirements, contact person name/phone/email of the responsible unit, bidder list, award decision and contract value. This is where organisational detail (which department owns core banking, which unit runs HR transformation) actually appears.

source_name: CS Ltd (CS Group) press centre / news — Ukrainian core-banking vendor (B2 / Б2, iFOBS)
source_subtype: vendor press centre / customer case studies
why_relevant: CS Ltd is the dominant domestic core-banking vendor in Ukraine (АБС Б2, iFOBS internet-banking). Its news feed names client banks, project completions and go-lives (e.g. project completion at Bank PIVDENNYI, migration of B2 user banks to the new NBU capital structure, 24/7 operating-day project). Vendor announcements are frequently the only public trace of a private bank's IT/organisation change, and they usually quote the client-side sponsor (CIO/deputy chairman), giving named leadership signals.

source_name: UNITY-BARS — banking software vendor (ABS BARS) corporate site
why_relevant: One of the two long-standing Ukrainian ABS vendors (founded 1996, ABS BARS). Customer/product pages and press coverage reveal which banks run BARS and which are migrating; the company also publicly discusses its own headcount and delivery organisation. Vendor-side migration news is a leading indicator of a private bank's IT reorganisation.

source_name: ProFIX — Ukrainian banking back-office / SEP software vendor
why_relevant: ProFIX/BANK and ProFIX/STAT serve NBU SEP/SSP connectivity and reporting for Ukrainian banks. Its client list and project notes indirectly map which private banks are re-platforming reporting/payments — a proxy for internal reorganisation and specialist hiring.

source_name: UPC — Ukrainian Processing Center (Raiffeisen Bank International group) corporate site & news
why_relevant: The largest non-bank card processor in Ukraine, serving many private banks and designated by the NBU as an important technological payment-services operator; it was also reported as the first Open Banking provider in Ukraine. Its client announcements, service launches and its own hiring/expansion (17-country footprint) are direct evidence of client-bank projects that never appear in bank procurement channels.

source_name: ProCard processing centre (Konkord Bank group)
why_relevant: One of the three universal Ukrainian non-bank processors. Client-bank onboarding announcements and service pages reveal which small/medium private banks outsource card processing — a structural organisation signal (in-house card IT wound down, vendor team scaled up).

source_name: PSM7.com — Ukrainian payments/fintech trade media, processing-market and TechFin coverage
why_relevant: Best single pointer source for the Ukrainian vendor/processor landscape: it publishes market overviews naming every processing centre and TechFin vendor serving banks, plus appointment and project news. Its overview articles are efficient actor-map builders that snowball into new vendor domains.

source_name: Fintech Insider UA — Ukrainian fintech/banking-tech news
why_relevant: Covers banking-technology programmes (e.g. Ukraine's ISO 20022 migration) that force vendor engagements and internal reorganisation across banks; useful for identifying which vendors and integrators are named around regulatory-driven IT programmes.

source_name: Banker.ua — projects/interviews section on banking infrastructure vendors
why_relevant: Publishes sponsored/interview 'projects' pieces where vendors and bank IT executives discuss infrastructure programmes; these pieces routinely name client-side sponsors and vendor delivery leads, which is exactly the leadership/organisation trace the private-bank indirect route needs.

source_name: OpenWay Group — customer stories, blog and presentations
why_relevant: Way4 is a major card/payment processing platform with a documented delivery footprint that includes Ukraine (project teams spread across 15+ countries incl. Ukraine). Customer success stories and go-live blogs name client institutions and sponsors; the corporate site is the canonical place where a Ukrainian bank win would surface.

source_name: BPC (SmartVista) — newsroom and Ukraine client announcements
why_relevant: BPC has an operational presence in Ukraine and a track record of announcing Ukrainian bank go-lives (e.g. Visa payWave launch at Credit Dnepr Bank on SmartVista, with a named board-level client quote). Exactly the vendor-benefits-from-announcing pattern this cell targets.

source_name: SoftServe careers — Ukraine vacancies feed
why_relevant: A paginated, country-filtered vacancy feed from the largest Ukrainian IT services firm. Financial-services role volume and city mix are a direct, high-frequency measure of delivery-centre expansion serving banks — an org-change signal for the sector, and job texts sometimes leak client-domain detail (core banking, cards, AML).

source_name: DOU.ua company profiles + jobs (jobs.dou.ua) for banking-IT vendors
why_relevant: DOU is the canonical Ukrainian IT community site: per-company pages carry vacancy counts, headcount trends, reviews and news, including for the banking-software vendors in this cell (e.g. UNITY-BARS has a company page). It is the single best local-language instrument for measuring vendor and bank in-house IT hiring in Ukraine.

source_name: IT Ukraine Association — member directory and Top-50 IT company rankings
why_relevant: Publishes the ranked list of the largest Ukrainian IT companies by specialist headcount, including the integrators serving banks (SoftServe, Ciklum, Infopulse, N-iX, EPAM). Headcount rankings over time are a clean org-change/expansion metric and the directory snowballs into vendor domains to monitor.

source_name: Ciklum — financial services vertical pages and careers
why_relevant: Ciklum (~3,000 specialists) runs a financial-services vertical serving retail banks and investment platforms and has published credit-risk/behavioural-analytics work. Its case studies, partner announcements and Ukraine vacancies indicate which bank-side capabilities are being built out through vendors.

source_name: Infopulse — banking/financial services case studies and news
why_relevant: Long-established Ukrainian engineering firm positioned for large-scale mission-critical projects including financial services; customer references and press releases are a route to identifying private-bank IT programmes and named client sponsors.

source_name: UkrCard — national payment infrastructure / integration products
why_relevant: Domestic card/integration infrastructure provider whose product and partner pages map which banks connect through it. Useful for the smaller private banks that never issue press releases of their own.

source_name: Softline IT (Kyiv) — system integrator, banking/ERP integration case notes
why_relevant: Local system integrator (since 1995) publishing project notes that reference integration work touching client banks (e.g. Dynamics 365 integration with client-bank systems at three major banks). Lower-tier but a genuine indirect trace of bank-side projects.

source_name: AppsRunTheWorld customer databases for Way4 and Oracle FLEXCUBE
why_relevant: Third-party aggregator listing named institutions running Way4 and FLEXCUBE. Useful as a cross-check to build the vendor-to-bank mapping when neither the bank nor the vendor publishes a release; must be treated as low-authority and corroborated.

source_name: NBU newsroom — payment-infrastructure operator designations and IT-programme milestones
why_relevant: Not a vendor source, but the regulator names the technological operators of payment services (this is how UPC's status is publicly established) and sets the deadlines (open banking from 1 Aug 2025, adaptation by 31 Dec 2025; ISO 20022) that trigger private-bank vendor engagements and team build-outs. Best pointer for timing vendor-side activity.

source_name: LinkedIn Ukraine (ua.linkedin.com) — people search / member profiles & posts
why_relevant: Individual bankers self-announce new roles, promotions, departures and new team/department creation before any institutional press release. Ukrainian banking/payments staff maintain profiles largely in English, with Ukrainian posts increasing since 2022.

source_name: LinkedIn company page — Raiffeisen Bank Ukraine
why_relevant: Bank-run page publishes welcome posts for new executives, internal reorganisation announcements and hiring campaigns; the 'People' tab shows headcount trend and function mix — a proxy for department creation.

source_name: LinkedIn company page — monobank (Universal Bank)
why_relevant: Fast-growing neobank; product/team posts frequently reveal new roles and squads earlier than press. Employee-authored posts snowball into individual profiles worth watching.

source_name: LinkedIn company page — PrivatBank
why_relevant: Largest UA retail bank and state-owned; management board turnover is frequent and often surfaces first as employee/executive posts and farewell notes.

source_name: LinkedIn company page — OTP Bank Ukraine
why_relevant: Foreign-owned group subsidiary; group-level appointments to the Ukrainian entity are frequently announced socially before local media.

source_name: LinkedIn company page — FUIB / ПУМБ
why_relevant: Top-5 private bank with an active employer-brand presence; posts surface new heads of function and hiring pushes.
